experiments.question: What exact instants and strings will simple-login.web's planned time functions (ADR-002 Decisions 4, 5 and 7, Intl only) give for booking-api@v1's fixtures under TZ=Asia/Kolkata, so the phase plan can state them?
experiments.finding: Intl alone implements every web-side rule: dayRange reproduces the three rooms fixtures' query paths exactly (London 2026-11-05, Jakarta 2026-11-05, London 2027-10-31 at 25 h); 2027-03-28 London is 23 h with 92 quarter hours and no 01:xx; 2027-10-31 has 100 with 01:00 to 01:45 BST then GMT. rooms-on-a-date for a London user reproduces PRD v2 Screens' Rooms lines; book-overlap for a Jakarta user gives 'Merapi is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00.'; marks read '01:00 GMT to 01:30 GMT', '23:30 to Mon 1 Nov 00:00', 'Wed 4 Nov 23:30 to 00:30' with '(Wed 4 Nov 16:30 to Wed 4 Nov 17:30 in London)'. Every 201 POST fixture's start and end are among the form's options with the browser clock at the fixture's clock, except book-started's (its clock reads the start). book-title-80-characters is 80 code points and 81 UTF-16 units. Intl accepts '+07:00' as a zone. The ambient zone under TZ=Asia/Kolkata resolves to 'Asia/Calcutta'.

routed.text: From S18 (DEC-172), carrying Q-064: simple-login.web's Overview says 'with three screens (PRD v2 Screens)', but PRD v2 Screens draws only Home and Rooms; the citation should read (PRD v2 US-1, Screens) so Login has its source. A phase-plan-append does not edit hsdd-spec's Overview, so this step left it; the segment's align, which makes citation changes only, or a later hsdd-spec touch on simple-login.web can make it. Nothing in the plan depends on it.

From S18 (simple-login.web's appended plan: D4, D7, D9, D10, D11; DEC-162, DEC-165, DEC-166, DEC-170), for the browser tests that select by visible text. Home: rows Username, Email, Phone, Time zone (the name as received, or 'Not available' without one), Member since; 'My bookings' with two lines per booking ('Thu 5 Nov  10:00 to 11:00', then 'Thames · Design review' and a 'Cancel' button), '(no bookings)' when empty; buttons 'Book a room' (only with a usable zone) and 'Sign out'. Rooms: heading 'Rooms on' with a YYYY-MM-DD date input that opens on today in the user's zone by the browser's clock, a 'Home' button, rooms as '{name} · {office} · {seats} seats', bookings as '{start} to {end}  {title}' plus '({start} to {end} in {office})' when the room's zone name differs. The form: selects for room, start and end, a title field and 'Book'; it leaves out starts the browser's clock has passed and ends past start + 8 hours or the next date's start, so BOOKING_STARTED through the UI needs the clock to pass the start between choosing and pressing Book. Messages: 'Booked.', AC-5.3's sentence, 'That time has already started.', 'A booking can last at most 8 hours.', 'A booking can start at most 365 days ahead.', 'That booking is not valid. Check the times and the title.'; on Cancel 'That booking has already started, so it cannot be cancelled.', 'That booking was already cancelled.', 'You can cancel only your own bookings.' Cancel shows on every listed booking, a started one included. A 401 at any booking call lands on Login with the AC-2.3 message. A reload on Rooms shows Home (no URL per screen). ADR-002 Decision 7's date mark is applied literally against the picked date, so a cross-date room-local line reads '(Wed 4 Nov 16:30 to Wed 4 Nov 17:30 in London)'. Exact strings per fixture: hsdd/auto/experiments/web-time-display/output.txt.

D11 offers ends up to start + 8 hours (DEC-166); the date input is deliberately not capped at 365 days, since the same date drives the read-only list and the backend decides. The confirm entry replaces the provisional consumer simple-login.web.5 with web.5, web.7, web.8 and web.9 (DEC-174).
